statement: Each of the 32 independent GPIO bits can be written as a peripheral output via direct write, giving software simultaneous control of all 32 bits.
Masked write modifies only the selected bits of a 16-bit half, using the user-provided mask and new values, without read-modify-write; unmasked bits keep their output value.
Software can read each of the 32 GPIO bits as peripheral inputs.
Software can configure interrupt event detection for any of the 32 bits as positive edge, negative edge or level detection.
The input must be stable for 16 module clock cycles before the input register reflects the change and interrupt generation is evaluated.
A change in output value is reflected in the input register with a corresponding filter delay.

not_verified.note: There is no pad model (INT-IO-002, D-021). i_gpio comes only from the test bench, so output-to-input delay does not occur. Designer decision for GP-T2.2-05/06.

statement: DIRECT_OUT provides full write and read access to all 32 bits of the DATA_OUT register.
Upper 16 bits of the write are a mask of bits to modify and lower 16 bits are data; hardware updates only masked DATA_OUT bits without read-modify-write.
Reads return the upper or lower 16 bits of DATA_OUT in the lower 16 bits, with zeros in the upper 16 mask-field bits.
DATA_OE is accessible directly via DIRECT_OE and with masked access via MASKED_OE_UPPER and MASKED_OE_LOWER, with the same semantics as DATA_OUT.
The output enable is sent to the pad control block to determine whether the pad drives the DATA_OUT value to the pin.
Output values of unused GPIOs are disconnected and have no effect on the GPIO input regardless of output enable values.
The per-pin and 32-bit register views alias the same state, and a write to a per-pin register affects only its own GPIO.

Per-pin view has separate aligned ranges: PER_PIN_IO holds one register per GPIO for DATA_OUT/DATA_IN bit i; configuration range holds consecutive PER_PIN_OE_n and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_n registers per GPIO.
A register write must cover all bytes of the register that hold a field.
INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST have no per-pin view.
DATA_IN is always readable and reflects the value at the chip input pad regardless of DATA_OE.
GPIO peripheral inputs not connected to a chip input are tied to constant zero.
Each of the 32 inputs can be independently enabled for the 16-cycle noise filter via CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER, applied to both DATA_IN and interrupt detection.
GPIO detects strap_en_i low-to-high and one clock cycle later samples the GPIO inputs into HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN.
All 32 input bits are sampled regardless of output enable, and later input changes are not captured in HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN.
Interrupt state is readable in INTR_STATE only when enabled, and can be triggered only by GPIO input.
Writing 1 to an INTR_STATE bit clears that interrupt.
Each bit supports rising-edge, falling-edge, level-high and level-low interrupt detection, selected by the corresponding INTR_CTRL_EN register.
An input may be configured for both rising and falling edge detection, with no hardware indication of which edge caused the interrupt.
All inputs pass through the optional noise filter before interrupt detection.
Interrupts to the processor are level interrupts; edge detection is converted into a level interrupt.
Each component should be granted access only to the per-pin registers of its own GPIOs, while software managing all GPIOs keeps using the 32-bit registers.

not_verified.note: Software capability-assignment advice; nothing to observe.

statement: A write to PER_PIN_IO_i must cover both bytes 0 and 1, i.e., be at least 16 bits wide.
A byte write to PER_PIN_IO_i returns an error and has no effect on the register.
PER_PIN_OE_i and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i accept byte writes.
gpio core registers INTR_STATE through HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN must be accessible at offsets 0x0 to 0x44 in 4-byte steps, each 4 bytes long, with the listed functions.
PER_PIN_IO_0 to PER_PIN_IO_31 must be at offsets 0x100 to 0x17c in 4-byte steps, each 4 bytes long, giving a per-pin view of output and input data of one GPIO.
PER_PIN_OE_n and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_n for GPIO[n], n=0..31, must alternate at offsets 0x200 to 0x2fc in 4-byte steps, each 4 bytes long.
INTR_STATE.gpio bit is raised when the corresponding GPIO pin detects its configured interrupt mode; the field is rw1c (write 1 clears).
Writing 1 to INTR_TEST.gpio[i] forces INTR_STATE.gpio[i] to 1.
Writing 0 to ALERT_TEST.regwen disables alert testing until the next reset.
Writing 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers one alert event of the fatal_fault kind.
Upper 16 bits of MASKED_OUT_LOWER are a mask; DATA_OUT[i] for i in 0..15 is updated with data[i] only if mask[i] is 1.
Reading MASKED_OUT_LOWER returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OUT[15:0].
Upper 16 bits of MASKED_OUT_UPPER are a mask; DATA_OUT[i] for i in 16..31 is updated from the lower 16 bits only if mask[i] is 1.
Reading MASKED_OUT_UPPER returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OUT[31:16].
Setting direct_oe[i] to 1 enables output mode for GPIO[i].
Upper 16 bits of MASKED_OE_LOWER are a mask; DATA_OE[i] for i in 0..15 is updated from the lower 16 bits only if mask[i] is 1.
Reading MASKED_OE_LOWER returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OE[15:0].
Upper 16 bits of MASKED_OE_UPPER are a mask; DATA_OE[i] for i in 16..31 is updated from the lower 16 bits only if mask[i] is 1.
Reading MASKED_OE_UPPER returns upper 16 bits as zero and lower 16 bits as DATA_OE[31:16].
Rising-edge interrupt detection on GPIO[i] is enabled.
Falling-edge interrupt detection on GPIO[i] is enabled.
Level-high interrupt detection on GPIO[i] is enabled.
Level-low interrupt detection on GPIO[i] is enabled.
A value of input bit [i] must be stable for 16 cycles before transitioning.
GPIO input data is sampled at most once after reset on the first cycle where strap_en_i is high, and stored in HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN.
HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN reads as zero.
PER_PIN_IO bit 8 (data_in) aliases DATA_IN[i] and bit 0 (data_out) aliases DATA_OUT[i] for GPIO[i].
Writing PER_PIN_IO updates only DATA_OUT[i], without affecting other GPIOs.
PER_PIN_OE_0 bit 0 aliases bit 0 of DIRECT_OE (DATA_OE[0]).
Writing PER_PIN_OE_0 updates only DATA_OE[0], without affecting other GPIOs.
PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_0 bits 0..4 alias bit 0 of INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING, FALLING, LVLHIGH, LVLLOW and CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER respectively.
Writing PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_0 updates only the configuration of GPIO[0], without affecting other GPIOs.
PER_PIN_OE_i at 0x200+8*i and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i at 0x204+8*i behave like the index-0 registers for GPIO[i], with reset default 0x0.

The behaviour of strap_en after the snapshot event must have no effect on the sampled strap values.
The corresponding gpio interrupt event must be raised when a GPIO pin detects the configured interrupt mode.
The fatal_fault alert must be triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected.
Every register access must be permitted and no access may be rejected for an access-control reason.
Ping requests must never be issued.

The response has d_error = 1 and no register changes.

statement: The bus carries at most one request and one response per cycle, and supports no burst transactions.

not_verified.note: gpio is not a baseline block.

not_verified.note: Relaxation for host drivers. The test bench follows D-016 (CHK-011).

not_verified.note: Interconnect routing rule. There is no fabric in ot_gpio_nnc.

statement: A host may use source ID bits to ascribe request identifiers, since TL-UL does not guarantee in-order responses.

The primitive shifts incoming a_source left and post-pends its sub-source bits.

statement: The sub-source bits are shifted off with zeros shifted into the top, and the result is returned on the originator's d_source.

statement: All lowRISC peripheral designs must conform to the register specification.

statement: A peripheral generates a separate wired interrupt for each interrupt source.

The event is latched into its INTR_STATE bitfield and intr_o goes high; a software W1C write clears it and intr_o goes low.

not_verified.note: Status-type interrupts. All gpio interrupts are event type (designer decision).
